author: cli
text: THESE GUARDS ARE THE ONLY DEFENCE THAT SURVIVES A COMPROMISED HOST, and the 0.55.1 bundle acceptance nearly proved nothing about them. All four attack falsifications (flipped byte, ../ traversal, symlink member, member outside .coord/) were served with the ORIGINAL .sha256 alongside the tampered tarball - so all four were refused by verify_checksum and this function never ran. Four green results, one guard actually tested. An attacker who can rewrite the tarball on the release host can rewrite the .sha256 next to it, so the checksum proves the bytes survived the wire, never that they are honest. Re-run with the checksum RECOMPUTED to match the payload, each of the three then failed HERE with its own message (escapes the target directory / is a link / lives outside .coord/), and nothing landed in /tmp or in the repo outside .coord/. GENERAL RULE: to test an inner guard you must neutralise the outer one, or the outer one answers in its place.
